fields.notes: Security in AMBA AHB and APB is limited to signaling primitives (HPROT / HNONSEC / PPROT / Exclusive Access / Lock + AHB5 parity) - not cryptographic primitives. End-to-end confidentiality/integrity must be provided by upper layers (TrustZone Address Space Controllers, MMU/SMMU, dedicated crypto IP, secure boot ROM). The specs explicitly note that the Data/Instruction bit is provided as a hint and is not accurate in all cases.

ahb_security_features.name: HPROT[1] Privileged
ahb_security_features.purpose: Privilege-level signaling for access control at the bus layer.

ahb_security_features.name: HEXCL + HMASTER + HEXOKAY (AHB5)
ahb_security_features.purpose: Exclusive Access mechanism for concurrency-safe RMW primitives.

ahb_security_features.name: HMASTLOCK
ahb_security_features.purpose: Locked-sequence indicator for atomic operations in multi-Manager configurations.

ahb_security_features.name: AHB5 Interface protection via parity (Chapter 12)
ahb_security_features.purpose: Single-bit fault detection on each interface.

what_is_NOT_in_the_specs: No confidentiality / encryption at the protocol layer.
No data-integrity / authentication (no MAC, no HMAC).
secure_integration_responsibilities: TrustZone partitioning via HNONSEC / PPROT[1] routed to Subordinate-side filters.
Master Security Wrappers enforce HNONSEC + HMASTER per Manager port.
PPROT[1] HIGH=Non-secure convention must be mirrored end-to-end.
